NotificationsService stores its data in **NotificationsRedisInstance**. That's the only thing it depends on. The graph has a single STORES relationship from NotificationsService to NotificationsRedisInstance, and nothing else, even when I searched three levels deep. It has no CALLS or DEPENDS_ON links to other services, APIs or databases.

The graph doesn't say **what** data NotificationsService puts in that Redis instance, because the STORES relationship has no details. Since it's Redis, it's likely holding short-lived data like queued notifications or delivery status, but that's a guess. To confirm, you'd need to check NotificationsService's code or config.

I didn't check configuration keys because the graph tool needs a specific key name to look up. If you know which key holds the Redis connection setting, I can look up what else uses it.
